    Point at Pages & Co. Books with a plain &: WordPress read the header without running a line. Installed, inactive, and that is right: there is nothing to run yet. Stop on the two requirement lines: they are the reason a PHP 8.1 server refuses the plugin politely (self-check Q1).
  3. Composer writes the autoloader (4m). "A namespace is the prefix for classes; PSR-4 is the rule that turns a class name into a file name." Write composer.json (learners copy it from the lesson), then run Composer in its container from the project folder: 
    {
	"name": "pagesco/pagesco-books",
	"description": "The bookstore features of the Pages & Co. website.",
	"type": "wordpress-plugin",
	"license": "GPL-2.0-or-later",
	"require": {
		"php": ">=8.2"
	},
	"autoload": {
		"psr-4": {
			"PagesCo\\Books\\": "src/"
		}
	}
}
    docker run --rm -it --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" -v "$PWD/wordpress:/var/www/html" -w /var/www/html/wp-content/plugins/pagesco-books composer:2 composer dump-autoload
    Composer could not detect the root package (pagesco/pagesco-books) version, defaulting to '1.0.0'. See https://getcomposer.org/root-version
Generating autoload files
Generated autoload files
    The first line is a harmless note (no version in composer.json). Windows PowerShell: no --user, ${PWD} (Lesson 1.3). Then Feature.php and Plugin.php: learners COPY these two from the lesson page; you read Plugin.php aloud with them: instance(), boot() with its own filter pagesco_books_features, feature(), and the empty list in feature_classes().
  4. Boot on plugins_loaded (3m). "Two lines finish the main file: load the autoloader, hand boot() to plugins_loaded." Append them, activate, and ask PHP two questions: 
    require PAGESCO_BOOKS_DIR . 'vendor/autoload.php';

add_action( 'plugins_loaded', array( PagesCo\Books\Plugin::instance(), 'boot' ) );

wp plugin activate pagesco-books
wp eval 'var_dump( has_action( "plugins_loaded", array( PagesCo\Books\Plugin::instance(), "boot" ) ), class_exists( "PagesCo\Books\Plugin", false ) );'
    Plugin 'pagesco-books' activated.
Success: Activated 1 of 1 plugins.
int(10)
bool(true)
    Hooked at priority 10, and the class is loaded (false = "do not autoload just for this question"). The plugin runs, with no features yet.
  5. A role through the life cycle (6m). "Three moments are different: activation, deactivation, uninstall." Copy Activator.php from the lesson, append the two register_*_hook() lines at the TOP LEVEL of the main file, write uninstall.php, then walk the role through all three: 
    register_activation_hook( __FILE__, array( PagesCo\Books\Activator::class, 'activate' ) );
register_deactivation_hook( __FILE__, array( PagesCo\Books\Activator::class, 'deactivate' ) );

wp role list --field=role | grep -c pagesco_bookseller

Success: Activated 1 of 1 plugins.
    Read the two numbers: deactivation kept the role (1), uninstall removed it (0), the last activation made it again. Write the life-cycle table on the board: activate = set up once · deactivate = pause, keep data · uninstall = remove the plugin's data.
  6. Mistake: a late activation hook (4m). "A tidy-minded developer moves everything into plugins_loaded, the activation hook too." Save the lesson's one-file demo plugin as wordpress/wp-content/plugins/pagesco-late-hook.php: 
    <?php
/**
 * Plugin Name: Late Hook Demo
 */

add_action(
	'plugins_loaded',
	function () {
		register_activation_hook( __FILE__, 'pagesco_late_hook_activate' );
	}
);

/**
 * Should run once, on activation.
 */
function pagesco_late_hook_activate() {
	update_option( 'pagesco_late_hook', 'activated' );
}
    wp plugin activate pagesco-late-hook
wp option get pagesco_late_hook
    Plugin 'pagesco-late-hook' activated.
Success: Activated 1 of 1 plugins.
Error: Could not get 'pagesco_late_hook' option. Does it exist?
    Activated, and the callback never ran: no option, no warning. On the activation request plugins_loaded fired BEFORE WordPress included the new file. Delete the demo: 
    wp plugin deactivate pagesco-late-hook
wp plugin delete pagesco-late-hook
    Plugin 'pagesco-late-hook' deactivated.
Success: Deactivated 1 of 1 plugins.
Deleted 'pagesco-late-hook' plugin.
Success: Deleted 1 of 1 plugins.
Three mistakes to expect, and how to coach each
  • A file name that does not match the class. storeNotice.php, Store_Notice.php, class-store-notice.php (Lesson 1.3's style). Coach: "Read the class name, swap PagesCo\Books\ for src/, add .php: is that the file?" (Self-check Q3; the psr4_paths lab.)
  • Hooks registered in the wrong place. The activation hook inside a callback; add_action( 'init', ... ) inside a class constructor that nothing creates. Coach: "Who calls this line, and when?" For features: only register() adds hooks, and boot() calls it. (Self-check Q6.)
  • Deleting data on deactivation. "Clean up" in deactivate(). Coach with the life-cycle line on the board: deactivate is a pause. (Self-check Q4; the gift_wrap lab's uninstall.php.)
Guided lab

Folder: labs/module-09/l5_1-first-plugin/gift_wrap_starter/ (a one-file plugin, pagesco-gift-wrap, plus its uninstall.php) with labs/module-09/l5_1-first-plugin/test_gift_wrap.sh; your reference is labs/module-09/l5_1-first-plugin/gift_wrap_solution/. It practices the whole life cycle on a plugin small enough to hold in your head: the requirement headers, the guard, an activation hook that stores an option once, a filter on the store notice of Lesson 2.3, and uninstall.php. It is not the lesson's project (that is StoreNotice in pagesco-books).

  • Install and run it as shipped (3m). cp -r labs/module-09/l5_1-first-plugin/gift_wrap_starter wordpress/wp-content/plugins/pagesco-gift-wrap, wp plugin activate pagesco-gift-wrap, copy the test into wordpress/ and docker compose run --rm wpcli sh test_gift_wrap.sh. Everything says TODO, the direct request is a 500 (no guard: the file runs without WordPress and dies on add_filter()), no price is stored.
  • TODOs 1 to 5 in pairs (10m). After editing, the activation hook must run again: wp plugin deactivate pagesco-gift-wrap && wp plugin activate pagesco-gift-wrap, then the test. The test ends with wp plugin uninstall --deactivate --skip-delete, so activate it again before the next run. Circulate for the activation hook written inside pagesco_gift_wrap_notice() and for get_option() without a check for false.

The lesson project is The First Feature Moves In: the two notice callbacks that Lesson 2.3 promised to move become the plugin's first feature. In the room: Steps 1 and 2 (15 minutes), on top of the skeleton from the demo.

Checks for understanding

Ask these out loud during the demo and the lab:

  • Which line makes a PHP file a plugin? Answer: a header comment with Plugin Name:; WordPress reads it without running the file.
  • What does defined( 'ABSPATH' ) || exit; stop? Answer: a direct request to the file from a browser, which would run it without WordPress.
  • Where does PagesCo\Books\Admin\SettingsPage live? Answer: src/Admin/SettingsPage.php, exactly that case.
  • What may deactivation never do? Answer: delete the owner's data; only uninstall.php does that.

Workbook self-check, items Q1 to Q6 (learners do them at the end of the block or at home).

Answers: Q1 B) WordPress refuses to activate it and says which PHP version the plugin requires; Q2 /var/www/html/wp-content/plugins/pagesco-books/; Q3 C) A fatal error: Class PagesCo\Books\Admin\BookColumns not found; Q4 A) Delete the Bookseller role and the plugin's options; Q5 NULL: uninstall.php removed the role, so get_role() finds nothing; Q6 D) Because on the activation request plugins_loaded has already fired before WordPress includes the new plugin's file. Full set with explanations in the Answer Key.

Differentiation

Support: a learner whose skeleton will not activate reads the error from the left with you: the file and line almost always point at a typo in the main file or a missing vendor/. If the demo ran away from them, copy all seven files from the lesson page at the break and run its checkpoint block.

Stretch: psr4_paths_starter.php, debug_plugin_audit.php; the lesson's Exercise 3 (switch a feature off from outside with pagesco_books_features) and the Bonus Challenge (a Features link on the Plugins screen).

5.2

Custom Post Types, Taxonomies & Meta

75 min
Objectives (from the lesson page)
  • Register a custom post type with register_post_type() on init, with labels, an archive and REST support
  • Register a custom taxonomy with register_taxonomy() and attach it to the post type
  • Register typed post meta with register_post_meta(), and explain why the keys are public and show_in_rest
  • Add a meta box and extra admin columns so editors can see and change a book's details
  • Flush rewrite rules at the right moment, and seed content safely with a WP-CLI script
Timing in the room
10mFrame: a new drawer in the same filing cabinet; type, taxonomy, meta; why rules need a flush
25mLive demo: the book type, the rules, the genre taxonomy, the activator, six meta keys, stale rules
15mGuided lab: book_quotes_starter/
15mStart the lesson project: Fill the Shelves, Steps 1 and 2 and the start of Step 3
Mental model to say

Back to Lesson 2.1's picture: "wp_posts is one big filing cabinet. A custom post type is a new labeled drawer in it, not a new cabinet: books are stored in the same table as posts and pages, with the same columns, so the Loop, WP_Query, revisions and the block editor work on them for free. A taxonomy is the colored tabs you clip onto the files to group them, a book's genres. Meta is the index card in each file with its own facts: this book's price, its author, its page count."

Then the three functions on the board, all called on init: register_post_type() (a kind of content: book), register_taxonomy() (a way to group it: genre), register_post_meta() (a named, typed field: pagesco_price). Each is one feature class in pagesco-books, the rule from Lesson 5.1.

Then the one thing that surprises everyone: "Registering a type adds URL rules, and WordPress keeps the rules in the database. Until something flushes them, /books/ is a 404." The activation hook gets its second job.

Live demo (you type, they follow)

On the site as Lesson 5.1 leaves it. Learners copy the three classes from the lesson page and type the sed and WP-CLI lines with you.

  1. The book post type (5m). "A custom post type is a new value in wp_posts.post_type: a new drawer in the same filing cabinet." Learners copy src/BookPostType.php from the lesson (it is mostly labels); you walk the arguments table: public, has_archive + rewrite, show_in_rest + rest_base, supports (custom-fields is required for meta in REST). List it: 
    sed -i '/StoreNotice::class,/a\			BookPostType::class,' wp-content/plugins/pagesco-books/src/Plugin.php
grep -n -A 3 "return array(" wp-content/plugins/pagesco-books/src/Plugin.php
    75:		return array(
76-			StoreNotice::class,

78-		);
    Note the NAME constant: no other file spells 'book'.
  2. Rules, and a flush (4m). "The type registers on every request now. Does /books/ work?" Ask for predictions (most say yes). It would 404: the rules in the database know nothing about books until something flushes them.

  5. Six meta keys (4m). "The index card in each file: author, price, pages." Copy src/BookMeta.php: the keys are DATA in fields(), one loop registers them. Stop on the box "Why the keys do not start with an underscore" (public keys for REST and block bindings). 
    sed -i '/GenreTaxonomy::class,/a\			BookMeta::class,' wp-content/plugins/pagesco-books/src/Plugin.php

  6. Mistake: stale rules (3m). "The commonest custom-post-type bug: the code is right and single books 404." Save the rules once without the type, then flush: 
    wp eval 'unregister_post_type( "book" ); flush_rewrite_rules();'
curl -s -o /dev/null -w 'before flush: %{http_code}\n' http://localhost:8080/books/
wp rewrite flush
curl -s -o /dev/null -w 'after flush:  %{http_code}\n' http://localhost:8080/books/
    before flush: 404
Success: Rewrite rules flushed.
after flush:  200
    An EMPTY rules option would not show the bug (WordPress rebuilds it); stale rules do. Fix: flush on activation, never on init (self-check Q10).
Three mistakes to expect, and how to coach each
  • "It's a 404, my code is wrong." Coach: "When did the rules last change? wp rewrite list --match=/books/." Then the fix in the right place: the activator. (Self-check Q10.)
  • The activator that only flushes. It trusts init to have registered the type; on the activation request it has not. Coach with the warning box "Registering is not enough on activation". (The book_quotes lab's TODO 4.)
  • Taxonomy or meta? A "genre" meta key, a "price" taxonomy. Coach with the lesson's test: "Would you want a page that lists everything with this value?" (Self-check Q9.)
Guided lab

Folder: labs/module-09/l5_2-custom-post-types/book_quotes_starter/ (a plugin, pagesco-quotes) with labs/module-09/l5_2-custom-post-types/test_book_quotes.sh; your reference is labs/module-09/l5_2-custom-post-types/book_quotes_solution/. A second post type, pagesco_quote, for favorite lines from the shop's books: learners make it public with an archive at /quotes/, put it in REST, register one public meta key, and write the activator that registers BEFORE it flushes. Same three functions as the lesson, on new data, in procedural style.

  • Install and run it as shipped (3m). cp -r labs/module-09/l5_2-custom-post-types/book_quotes_starter wordpress/wp-content/plugins/pagesco-quotes, wp plugin activate pagesco-quotes, copy the test, run it: the archive is a 404 and REST says rest_no_route.
  • TODOs 1 to 4 in pairs (9m). After each change: deactivate and activate the plugin (the activator must run), then the test. Circulate for has_archive => true (the archive is then /pagesco_quote/), for a meta key without show_in_rest, and for an activator that calls flush_rewrite_rules() alone.
  • Expected when done (the solution's test):
Plugin 'pagesco-quotes' activated.
Success: Activated 1 of 1 plugins.
archive /quotes/: 200
REST /wp/v2/quotes:
[{"title":{"rendered":"A truth universally acknowledged"},"meta":{"pagesco_quote_source":"Pride and Prejudice"}}]
quotes left: 0
  • Debrief (3m): "What did the activator have to do that init does on every other request?" (register first). "Why is the meta key in REST without a leading underscore?" (a protected key cannot be written through REST without an auth callback, and block bindings refuse it).
  • Fast finishers: labs/module-09/l5_2-custom-post-types/debug_meeting_type.php (three registration bugs). shelf_report_starter.php needs the seeded catalog: it is homework after the project.
  • Remove it afterwards: wp plugin deactivate pagesco-quotes, then rm -r wordpress/wp-content/plugins/pagesco-quotes wordpress/test_book_quotes.sh (deactivation unregisters the type and flushes the rules again).

Checks for understanding

Ask these out loud during the demo and the lab:

  • Where are books stored? Answer: in wp_posts, with post_type book; their meta in wp_postmeta; genres in the term tables.
  • Why does the activator register the type itself? Answer: on the activation request the plugin's own init callback has not run, so the rules would be flushed without the type.
  • Why pagesco_price and not _pagesco_price? Answer: an underscore key is protected: hidden from the Custom Fields box, not writable through REST without an auth callback, refused by block bindings.
  • What happens to the books when the plugin is deactivated? Answer: they stay in the database; the type is unregistered, so they vanish from the admin and their URLs 404 until it is active again.

Workbook self-check, items Q7 to Q12 (learners do them at the end of the block or at home).

Answers: Q7 B) /books/; Q8 '' (an empty string); Q9 A) As a taxonomy on the book type; Q10 D) It rewrites the whole rules option on every page load: a needless, slow database write; Q11 [{"title":{"rendered":"The Hobbit"}},{"title":{"rendered":"Lord of the Rings"}}]; Q12 C) wp_set_object_terms( $id, $genres, 'genre' ) after the insert. Full set with explanations in the Answer Key.

Differentiation

Support: learners who fell behind in the demo copy the three classes and the activator from the lesson page and run its sed blocks in order; the project's seeding script tells them if the type or taxonomy is missing. Pair them with someone whose wp post-type list shows book.

Stretch: debug_meeting_type.php, then (after seeding) shelf_report_starter.php; the lesson's Exercise 4 (one more meta key from a throwaway must-use plugin) and the Bonus Challenge (a sortable Price column).

Closing

Exit ticket (3 questions, no notes, 4 minutes)

Put the three questions on the slide. Learners answer in the workbook's Exit Ticket box or on a sticky note. Sort the notes before Session 10: question 2's "not yet" pile tells you how much of the warm-up goes to the life cycle.

  1. Name the three files every new pagesco-books feature touches, and what each gets. Answer: a new class in src/ that implements Feature (its hooks in register()), one line in Plugin::feature_classes(), and (if it stores data) a line in uninstall.php.
  2. What does each moment do to the Bookseller role: activation, deactivation, uninstall? Answer: creates it, keeps it, removes it.
  3. /books/ is a 404 right after you registered the book type. Why, and where does the permanent fix go? Answer: the rewrite rules in the database were saved before the type existed; flush them, and flush in the activator (after registering the type) from then on.
Homework (about 2 to 3 hours)
  • Finish both lesson projects. 5.1: Steps 3 and 4 (the missing class on purpose, the final check, the line in pagesco-plan.txt). 5.2: "Seeing Books in the Admin" (BookMetaBox and BookColumns) and Steps 3 and 4 (the column check, then rm -r pagesco-seed). Session 10 starts from exactly this site.
  • Lesson exercises. 5.1: Exercises 1 to 3 (an old server, a feature the plugin's way, switching a feature off); Exercise 4 is a stretch. 5.2: Exercises 1 to 3 (by author, by genre, the safe re-run); Exercise 4 is a stretch.
  • Both Quick Quizzes on the lesson pages (answers in the Answer Key).
  • Journal: both entries. The 5.1 prompt asks for the next three features as class names: keep the list, Sessions 10 and 11 build three of them.
  • Labs not reached: labs/module-09/l5_1-first-plugin/psr4_paths_starter.php, labs/module-09/l5_1-first-plugin/debug_plugin_audit.php, labs/module-09/l5_2-custom-post-types/debug_meeting_type.php, and after the project labs/module-09/l5_2-custom-post-types/shelf_report_starter.php.
  • Before the Next Lesson (from 5.2): pagesco-books lists six features, eleven books are published, /books/ and /genre/fiction/ load, and the Book details box shows on a book.
Bring list for Session 10
  • A laptop whose Part 2 check says READY (or READY WITH NOTES), with the site at the end of Lesson 5.2: wp post list --post_type=book --format=count prints 11 and the Book details box is on the book screen.
  • Two browsers or a private window: Session 10 logs in as admin, maria (editor) and devon (author) side by side.
  • The project folder with labs/, pagesco-plan.txt, the journal and the workbook.

If You Run Long or Short

Running long: what to protect and what to cut first
  • Protect: the Part 2 check result for every learner; a working 5.1 skeleton on every machine; the 5.1 life cycle; the 5.2 flush.
  • Cut first (saves 4m): the 5.1 late-hook mistake: point at Common Mistakes 3 on the page.
  • Cut second (saves 3m): the 5.2 genre step: learners copy GenreTaxonomy.php and run its block at the start of the project.
  • Cut third (saves 15m): the 5.2 project start: the seeding script is eight minutes at home and the lesson prints every output.
Running short: what to add
  • Lesson 5.1's Common Mistakes 2 live (rename vendor/, activate, read the stack trace: plugin_sandbox_scrape() is the useful frame), then put it back.
  • Lesson 5.1's Exercise 3 together: switch StoreNotice off from a must-use plugin with the plugin's own filter.
  • Lesson 5.2's Common Mistakes 3: the REST API refusing "lots" as a page count, and the draft it leaves behind.
Instructor Kit · Facilitator Guide

Session 10: Security and the Settings API

How to teach Session 10. Make the pagesco-books plugin safe with the four habits of WordPress security (sanitize in, escape out, a nonce for genuine requests, a capability for allowed users) and $wpdb->prepare(), showing each attack turn into a dead end on the course site, then give the shop a settings page with the Settings API, trace a save through options.php, and let the store notice read the settings.

2 lessons 3 hrs session Lessons 5.3–5.4 Session 10 of 18 · Part 2

How to Use This Guide

  • Same rhythm for both lessons: frame (the goal and one mental model) → live demo (you type, they type along) → guided lab (a kit lab, new practice on the lesson's ideas) → start the lesson's own project. The lesson exercises, quiz and journal are homework.
  • Every command below was run to produce the output printed under it, on WordPress 7.1.3 / PHP 8.5: the 5.3 demo on the site as Lesson 5.2 leaves it (after:lesson_15), the 5.4 demo on the site as Lesson 5.3 leaves it. Ask for a prediction before every run and read every message from the left.
  • Type the short things, copy the long ones (Session 9's rule): learners type the WP-CLI lines and the sed lines; they copy BookMetaBox.php, StockAction.php, Settings.php, SettingsPage.php and pagesco-save.sh from the lesson pages, then read them aloud with you.
  • Keep lesson_16.html and lesson_17.html open in browser tabs. Labs live in labs/module-10/: _starter files are handouts, _solution files are yours.
  • Two browsers. Today logs in as admin, maria (editor, maria-pass) and devon (author, devon-pass). A normal and a private window on the projector make the capability demos visible.
The #1 risk of Session 10: security as a list of rules

Five functions, four habits and six vulnerabilities fit on one slide and leave nobody's head the next day. The cure is the lesson's own method: every defense is shown turning a working attack into a dead end, on this very site. Do the attacks for real (the stored script tag, the forged request, the wrong user), keep the data flow drawing on the board all session (genuine? allowed? sanitize → store → escape), and send every learner question back to it: "which of the five boxes is this?" Lesson 5.4 then shows the same five boxes, built into options.php.

Before the Session

  • ☐ Homework check by email or at the door: wp post list --post_type=book --format=count prints 11, and the Book details box shows on a book (Lesson 5.2's "Seeing Books in the Admin"). Lesson 5.3 replaces that meta box's save: without it, Step 1 of the project has nothing to harden.
  • ☐ Run the kit check once: python3 labs/check_labs.py module-10 (12 results in about a minute; every line PASS). With your own course project: WP_LABS_COMPOSE=~/pagesco-dev python3 labs/check_labs.py module-10.
  • ☐ Projector machine at the end of Lesson 5.2 (after:lesson_15): eleven books, six features. Two browser windows: admin in one, maria in a private window; lesson_16.html and lesson_17.html in tabs; a terminal for tail -f wordpress/wp-content/debug.log.
  • ☐ Board, before learners arrive: the data flow request → genuine? (nonce) → allowed? (capability) → sanitize → store → escape → page; the escaping table (text esc_html · attribute esc_attr · link esc_url · allowed HTML wp_kses_post); the two names that look alike, group pagesco_books and page slug pagesco-books.
  • ☐ Print or share: the workbook, sticky notes for the exit ticket.
Known traps of Session 10
SymptomCauseFix
"The link you followed has expired." on a real clickThe link was built without wp_nonce_url(), or with a different action string than check_admin_referer()The same action string on both sides: self::ACTION . '_' . $post->ID.
The meta box no longer saves anythingThe save returns at the nonce check: the field name differs between render() and save()pagesco_books_details_nonce in both; wp_nonce_field( action, name ).
Error: The pagesco-books options page is not in the allowed options list.settings_fields() got the page slug instead of the groupsettings_fields( Settings::GROUP ); do_settings_sections( self::SLUG ) (5.4, Common Mistakes 1).
Warning: Undefined array key "show_events_link" in debug.log on saveThe sanitize callback reads an unticked checkbox! empty( $input['show_events_link'] ) (Common Mistakes 2).
The notice sentence vanished after a WP-CLI changeupdate_option() with half the arraySave the form again (or wp option patch update ...).
pagesco-save.sh prints options.php answered: 200 and an error pageNot logged in (wrong password) or the plugin is inactiveadmin / password; wp plugin list.
Maria sees the settings pageA capability other than manage_options (edit_posts, read)The capability is for what the page can change: manage_options.

Lesson Plans

5.3

Security in WordPress

70 min
Objectives (from the lesson page)
  • Sanitize input on the way in and escape output on the way out, choosing the right function for each context
  • Protect every state change with a nonce and a current_user_can() capability check
  • Write safe database queries with $wpdb->prepare() and explain how SQL injection works
  • Name the common WordPress vulnerabilities (XSS, CSRF, SQL injection, broken access control) and the defense against each
  • Harden a real save handler and an admin action in the pagesco-books plugin
Timing in the room
10mFrame: the shop's back door; the data flow; the four habits plus prepare()
30mLive demo: escaping, sanitizers, the nonce, a prepared query, three mistakes
15mGuided lab: staff_note_starter.php in pairs
15mStart the lesson project: Steps 1 and 2
Mental model to say

"Your plugin's write handlers are the shop's back door, where deliveries come in. A nonce is checking the delivery has the token you handed the courier this morning, so it is not a stranger with a forged clipboard. The capability check is making sure the person signing for it works here. Sanitizing is unwrapping and inspecting the goods before they go on the shelf. Escaping is how you display a customer's name in the window: you print it as text, never as a sign someone else wrote for you. Skip any one step and the shop is exposed in a different way."

Then the flow on the board, one box per habit, left to right: request → genuine? (nonce) → allowed? (capability) → sanitize → store → escape → page, and under the store box: SQL by hand → $wpdb->prepare(). Every demo step below lands in one box: say which before you run it.

And one sentence on where WordPress helps: "The block editor and the REST API check nonces and capabilities for you. The moment you write your own form handler, admin action or AJAX endpoint, those checks are your job."

Live demo (you type, they follow)

On the site as Lesson 5.2 leaves it. Learners type along; ask for a prediction before every run.

  1. A stored script tag, escaped (4m). "Every value from outside is untrusted. The author of a book comes from a form." Set Dune's author to a string full of HTML and print it the way the Books column does: 
    wp post meta update 30 pagesco_author 'Herbert & Sons <script>alert(1)</script>'
wp eval 'ob_start(); do_action( "manage_book_posts_custom_column", "pagesco_author", 30 ); echo ob_get_clean(), "\n";'
wp post meta update 30 pagesco_author 'Frank Herbert'
    Success: Updated custom field 'pagesco_author'.
Herbert &amp; Sons &lt;script&gt;alert(1)&lt;/script&gt;
Success: Updated custom field 'pagesco_author'.
    Entities, not tags: esc_html() in BookColumns::print_column() did its job, and the last command put the real author back. Show the anti-example from the lesson (the same column without escaping) and say: "Stored XSS runs for every editor who opens the Books list."
  2. Sanitizers at work (3m). "Escaping protects output; sanitizing protects what you store." Three deliberately bad inputs: 
    wp eval '$in = array( "price" => "-5.50", "pages" => "412 pages", "author" => "O\x27Brien <b>Press</b>" );
echo "price:  ", max( 0, (float) $in["price"] ), "\n";
echo "pages:  ", absint( $in["pages"] ), "\n";
echo "author: ", sanitize_text_field( $in["author"] ), "\n";'
    price:  0
pages:  412
author: O'Brien Press
    Then the two gaps in Lesson 5.2's save, on the board: autosaves (no form fields, would wipe the values) and validating a date, not just cleaning it.
  3. The nonce round trip (3m). "Is this request genuine?" The two functions behind every form token: 
    wp eval 'wp_set_current_user( 2 );
$token = wp_create_nonce( "pagesco_books_save_details" );
echo "verify good token: ", var_export( (bool) wp_verify_nonce( $token, "pagesco_books_save_details" ), true ), "\n";
echo "verify bad token:  ", var_export( (bool) wp_verify_nonce( "deadbeef", "pagesco_books_save_details" ), true ), "\n";'
    verify good token: true
verify bad token:  false
    In a form you never call them by hand: wp_nonce_field() prints the field, check_admin_referer() verifies it and stops with a 403. Then the second question, separately: current_user_can().
  4. A prepared query (4m). "When you write SQL by hand, every value goes through a placeholder." Show the anti-example (concatenation) first, then run the safe report and read the SQL prepare() built: 
    wp eval 'global $wpdb;
$author    = "Frank Herbert";
$max_price = 20;
$sql = $wpdb->prepare(
    "SELECT p.post_title, pm_price.meta_value AS price
     FROM {$wpdb->posts} p
     INNER JOIN {$wpdb->postmeta} pm_author ON pm_author.post_id = p.ID AND pm_author.meta_key = \"pagesco_author\"
     INNER JOIN {$wpdb->postmeta} pm_price  ON pm_price.post_id  = p.ID AND pm_price.meta_key  = \"pagesco_price\"
     WHERE p.post_type = %s AND pm_author.meta_value = %s AND pm_price.meta_value + 0 <= %d",
    "book",
    $author,
    $max_price
);
echo $sql, "\n---\n";
foreach ( $wpdb->get_results( $sql ) as $row ) { echo $row->post_title, " $", $row->price, "\n"; }'
    SELECT p.post_title, pm_price.meta_value AS price
     FROM wp_posts p
     INNER JOIN wp_postmeta pm_author ON pm_author.post_id = p.ID AND pm_author.meta_key = "pagesco_author"
     INNER JOIN wp_postmeta pm_price  ON pm_price.post_id  = p.ID AND pm_price.meta_key  = "pagesco_price"
     WHERE p.post_type = 'book' AND pm_author.meta_value = 'Frank Herbert' AND pm_price.meta_value + 0 <= 20
---
Dune $14.99
    'Frank Herbert' was quoted, 20 went in as a number. One rule: no variable ever goes directly into a query string.
  5. Mistake: the wrong context (2m). "Escaping is not one function." 
    wp eval '$url = home_url( "/books/?genre=sci-fi&sort=price" );
echo "esc_url:  ", esc_url( $url ), "\n";
echo "esc_html: ", esc_html( $url ), "\n";'
    esc_url:  http://localhost:8080/books/?genre=sci-fi&#038;sort=price
esc_html: http://localhost:8080/books/?genre=sci-fi&amp;sort=price
    esc_url() keeps a usable link (the & becomes &#038; for an attribute); esc_html() turns it into display text.
  6. Mistake: a nonce but no capability (2m). "A nonce proves the request is genuine, not that the user is allowed." 
    wp eval 'wp_set_current_user( 2 );
echo "editor edit Dune (30):   ", var_export( current_user_can( "edit_post", 30 ), true ), "\n";
wp_set_current_user( 3 );
echo "author edit Dune (30):   ", var_export( current_user_can( "edit_post", 30 ), true ), "\n";'
    editor edit Dune (30):   true
author edit Dune (30):   false
  7. Mistake: trusting an insert (2m). "Database functions assume you already checked." 
    wp eval 'wp_set_current_user( 3 );
$id = wp_insert_post( array( "post_type" => "book", "post_title" => "Snuck in", "post_status" => "publish" ) );
echo "created book as author Devon: ", ( $id ? "ID $id" : "failed" ), "\n";
wp_delete_post( $id, true );'
    created book as author Devon: ID 41
    An author created a published book (ID 41); the last line deleted it. Broken access control without any error message.
Three mistakes to expect, and how to coach each
  • Escaping at input instead of output. esc_html() in the save, raw echo in the column. Coach: "Where does the value land? Escape there, at the last moment, even if you sanitized it." (Self-check Q1, Q2.)
  • One check standing in for another. A nonce instead of a capability, a capability instead of a nonce, is_admin() as a permission check (it only says the request is for an admin screen). Coach with the flow: "Which box does this function fill?" (Self-check Q3, Q5.)
  • Sanitizing a value that needs validating. A date run through sanitize_text_field(). Coach: "Clean it, or judge it?" (Self-check Q6.)
Guided lab

File: labs/module-10/l5_3-security/staff_note_starter.php; your reference is labs/module-10/l5_3-security/staff_note_solution.php. A save handler for a private staff note on a book, attacked by four requests the script plays as different users: no token, a forged token, the wrong user (Devon may not edit Dune) and a script tag from the right user. As shipped it saves everything. Learners add the nonce check, the capability check and the sanitizing in the order the lesson's hardened save uses.

  • Run it as shipped (3m). cp labs/module-10/l5_3-security/staff_note_starter.php wordpress/ then wp eval-file --use-include staff_note_starter.php: four times saved, the last one with <script> stored.
  • TODOs 1 to 4 in pairs (9m). Circulate for the nonce action string (it must be the one the form was made with: 'pagesco_lab_note_' . $post_id), for current_user_can( 'edit_post' ) without the post ID, and for escaping instead of sanitizing.
  • Expected when done:
no token, as Maria              refused: no token    stored: (nothing)
forged token, as Maria          refused: bad token   stored: (nothing)
real token, as Devon            refused: not allowed stored: (nothing)
real token, as Maria, with tag  saved                stored: Signed copy, ask at the counter.
  • Debrief (3m): "Which request would a CSRF attack send?" (the forged token). "Why does Devon have a REAL token and still fail?" (he may open the form; he may not edit this book). "And the script tag?" (sanitize_text_field() stripped it; the column would still escape on output).
  • Fast finishers: labs/module-10/l5_3-security/prepared_search_starter.php (placeholders, LIKE and a hostile value), then labs/module-10/l5_3-security/debug_book_search.php (two misused prepare() calls and a silent bug).
Start the lesson project

The lesson project is Harden the Plugin: the real meta box save, and a "Mark sold out" row action built the safe way. In the room: Steps 1 and 2 (15 minutes).

  • Step 1: learners replace BookMetaBox.php with the lesson's hardened version (copy it) and read the four numbered checks in save() aloud: real submission, not an autosave; our nonce; may edit this book; sanitize and validate. Check it:
php -l wp-content/plugins/pagesco-books/src/Admin/BookMetaBox.php
wp eval '$GLOBALS["current_screen"] = WP_Screen::get( "book" );
do_action( "add_meta_boxes_book", get_post( 30 ) );
echo isset( $GLOBALS["wp_meta_boxes"]["book"]["normal"]["high"]["pagesco-book-details"] ) ? "Book details box registered\n" : "missing\n";'
No syntax errors detected in wp-content/plugins/pagesco-books/src/Admin/BookMetaBox.php
Book details box registered
  • Step 2: StockAction.php (copy it): the link built with wp_nonce_url() and only for users who may edit the book; the handler with check_admin_referer(), the capability, wp_safe_redirect(). List it and check who sees the link:
sed -i '/Admin\\BookColumns::class,/a\			Admin\\StockAction::class,' wp-content/plugins/pagesco-books/src/Plugin.php
wp eval 'wp_set_current_user( 2 );
$a = apply_filters( "post_row_actions", array(), get_post( 30 ) );
echo "editor sees stock action: ", isset( $a["pagesco_stock"] ) ? "yes\n" : "no\n";
wp_set_current_user( 3 );
$a = apply_filters( "post_row_actions", array(), get_post( 30 ) );
echo "author sees stock action: ", isset( $a["pagesco_stock"] ) ? "yes\n" : "no\n";'
editor sees stock action: yes
author sees stock action: no
  • Done in the room = the box registered and the link for the editor only. Goes home: Step 3 (the forged request: a 403 "The link you followed has expired.", and the checkpoint), then a real click on "Mark sold out" in the browser.
Checks for understanding

Ask these out loud during the demo and the lab:

  • When do you escape? Answer: at the point of output, for the context it lands in.
  • What does a nonce prove, and what does it not? Answer: that the request came from a page this site served to this user; not that the user is allowed.
  • Does wp_insert_post() check capabilities? Answer: no; check current_user_can() yourself first.
  • Why does the save skip autosaves? Answer: an autosave carries no form fields and would wipe the stored values.

Workbook self-check, items Q1 to Q6 (learners do them at the end of the block or at home).

Answers: Q1 C) esc_attr(); Q2 Pride &amp; Prejudice &lt;2nd ed.&gt;; Q3 B) The request came from a page this site served to this user, for this action, recently; Q4 SELECT ID FROM wp_posts WHERE post_title = 'Ender\'s Game'; Q5 A) current_user_can( 'edit_post', $book_id ) before the update; Q6 D) Validating it: DateTime::createFromFormat( 'Y-m-d', $v ) must give back exactly $v, else store ''. Full set with explanations in the Answer Key.

Differentiation

Support: a learner lost in the functions gets one card: out = esc_* · in = sanitize_* · genuine = nonce · allowed = current_user_can · SQL = prepare. Pair them on the lab with the flow drawing in front of them.

Stretch: prepared_search_starter.php, debug_book_search.php; the lesson's Exercise 2 (esc_js) and Exercise 4 (a capability-gated bulk change), and the Bonus Challenge (a Duplicate row action).

5.4

Admin Pages, Settings API & Options

75 min
Objectives (from the lesson page)
  • Store a plugin's settings as one array option with defaults, and read it safely with get_option() and wp_parse_args()
  • Add an admin page with add_options_page() (or a top-level menu) protected by the right capability
  • Build a settings form with the Settings API: register_setting(), sections, fields, settings_fields() and do_settings_sections()
  • Validate submitted values in a sanitize callback and report problems with add_settings_error()
  • Trace what happens between Save Changes and the database: options.php, the nonce, the allowed options list
  • Decide what uninstall.php removes, and remove the plugin's own settings
Timing in the room
10mFrame: one labeled box on the shared shelf; menus and capabilities; the Settings API as data
30mLive demo: Settings, the page and its 403, the form, the save round trip, half an array
15mGuided lab: newsletter_settings_starter/
20mStart the lesson project: Steps 1 and 2
Mental model to say

"wp_options is a shelf in the back office that every plugin shares. You could put each of your settings on it loose, four little notes with your name on them, or one labeled box, pagesco_books_settings, with all your notes inside. One box is easier to find, to load in one go, and to throw away when you leave."

Then the Settings API in four pieces on the board, next to Lesson 5.3's flow: register_setting() (the option, its group, its sanitize callback, its default) · add_settings_section() / add_settings_field() (the form as data, on admin_init) · settings_fields() + do_settings_sections() + submit_button() (the form on your page) · options.php (core's handler: nonce, capability, allowed list, update_option(), your callback). "Lesson 5.3's five boxes, built in."

And the two names that look alike, circled: group pagesco_books (settings_fields) and page slug pagesco-books (do_settings_sections, the URL).

On the site as Lesson 5.3 leaves it, with admin in one browser and maria in a private window.

<tr><th scope="row"><label for="pagesco-books-per-page">Books per list</label></th><td><input type="number" id="pagesco-books-per-page" name="pagesco_books_settings[books_per_page]" value="6" min="1" max="24" step="1" class="small-text"></td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row"><label for="pagesco-events-limit">Events to show</label></th><td><input type="number" id="pagesco-events-limit" name="pagesco_books_settings[events_limit]" value="5" min="1" max="20" step="1" class="small-text"></td></tr>
    Inputs named pagesco_books_settings[...]: that array syntax makes PHP deliver the four values as one array, stored as one option.
  5. What Save Changes does (6m). "Press Save Changes, or let a script do exactly what the browser does." Save the lesson's pagesco-save.sh in the WordPress root (copy it), then send the four fields with an Events value the callback must refuse: 
    sh pagesco-save.sh 'pagesco_books_settings[notice_extra]=Open until 9 p.m. on Thursdays.' 'pagesco_books_settings[show_events_link]=1' 'pagesco_books_settings[books_per_page]=8' 'pagesco_books_settings[events_limit]=50'
wp option get pagesco_books_settings
    options.php answered: 302 http://localhost:8080/wp-admin/options-general.php?page=pagesco-books&settings-updated=true
Events to show must be between 1 and 20.
array (
  'notice_extra' => 'Open until 9 p.m. on Thursdays.',
  'show_events_link' => true,
  'books_per_page' => 8,
  'events_limit' => 5,
)
    Read from the top: 302 = nonce, capability and allowed options list passed; your error instead of "Settings saved."; Books per list stored as 8, Events to show kept at 5. Draw the options.php flow from the lesson's diagram on the board.
  6. Mistake: half an array from code (3m). "The form always sends every field. Code does not have to." 
    wp eval 'update_option( "pagesco_books_settings", array( "events_limit" => 8 ) );'
wp option get pagesco_books_settings
    array (
  'notice_extra' => '',
  'show_events_link' => false,
  'books_per_page' => 8,
  'events_limit' => 8,
)
    The sentence is now empty and the link is off, with no error anywhere: update_option() replaced the whole value and the callback treated every missing key as empty. Put the form's values back: 
    sh pagesco-save.sh 'pagesco_books_settings[notice_extra]=Open until 9 p.m. on Thursdays.' 'pagesco_books_settings[show_events_link]=1' 'pagesco_books_settings[books_per_page]=6' 'pagesco_books_settings[events_limit]=5'
    options.php answered: 302 http://localhost:8080/wp-admin/options-general.php?page=pagesco-books&settings-updated=true
Settings saved.
Three mistakes to expect, and how to coach each
  • The group and the slug swapped. "not in the allowed options list". Coach: "settings_fields() takes the FIRST argument of register_setting()." (Lesson quiz Q1.)
  • A sanitize callback that returns only what changed, or $input unchanged. Coach: "It returns the complete value to store; what happens to a key you leave out?" (Self-check Q10; the newsletter lab's TODO 2.)
  • The wrong capability. edit_posts so editors can "help". Coach: "What can this page change? Site-wide behavior: manage_options." (Self-check Q11.)

Start the lesson project

The lesson project is Settings the Shop Can Change: the store notice reads the settings, the staff change it from the admin, and uninstalling cleans up. In the room: Steps 1 and 2 (20 minutes).

  • Step 1: replace StoreNotice.php with the lesson's version (the callbacks keep their names; only their bodies change). With the saved values equal to the defaults, the notice must look as it has since Lesson 2.3:
http://localhost:8080/   (View Source: the notice)

sh pagesco-save.sh 'pagesco_books_settings[notice_extra]=Signed copies of <b>Dune</b> this week.' 'pagesco_books_settings[books_per_page]=6' 'pagesco_books_settings[events_limit]=5'

  • The new sentence without the tags (sanitize_text_field() removed them on the way in) and no link. Nobody touched PHP. Then put the usual notice back the same way.

Checks for understanding

Ask these out loud during the demo and the lab:

  • Why does wp option get pagesco_books_settings answer although the table has no row? Answer: register_setting()'s default is handed out while the row is missing.
  • Where does the form post, and what does that file check? Answer: wp-admin/options.php: the nonce, manage_options, the allowed options list; then it saves through your sanitize callback.
  • What arrives for an unticked checkbox? Answer: nothing; missing means off.
  • What should uninstall.php do with the settings option, and with the books? Answer: delete the option (the plugin's own); keep the books (the shop's content).

Workbook self-check, items Q7 to Q12 (learners do them at the end of the block or at home).

Answers: Q7 A) Core's own handler, wp-admin/options.php, before it calls your sanitize callback; Q8 {"notice_extra":"Open until 9 p.m. on Thursdays.","show_events_link":true,"books_per_page":6,"events_limit":5}; Q9 C) Nothing: an unticked checkbox is not sent at all; Q10 {"notice_extra":"","show_events_link":false,"books_per_page":6,"events_limit":7}: 0 is out of range, so books_per_page keeps the saved value (6, the default); notice_extra and show_events_link were not in the array, so they come back empty and false; Q11 D) The manage_options capability passed to add_options_page(); Q12 B) A counter of page views, updated on every request. Full set with explanations in the Answer Key.

Differentiation

Support: learners who fall behind copy Settings.php and the full SettingsPage.php, run the two sed lines, and open the page in the browser: the form is the feedback. The newsletter lab then repeats every piece on a smaller scale.

Stretch: debug_newsletter_sanitize.php and settings_probe_starter.php; the lesson's Exercise 2 (a stylesheet only on your page), Exercise 4 (the settings in REST) and the Bonus Challenge (Reset to defaults).

Closing

Exit ticket (3 questions, no notes, 4 minutes)

Put the three questions on the slide. Learners answer in the workbook's Exit Ticket box or on a sticky note. Before Session 11, sort question 1's notes: anyone who cannot name the four checks gets the support card in the warm-up.

  1. Name the four checks a handler that changes data makes, in order. Answer: genuine (nonce: check_admin_referer() / wp_verify_nonce()), allowed (current_user_can() for this object), sanitize and validate every value, and escape whatever it prints; SQL by hand through $wpdb->prepare().
  2. What does options.php do between Save Changes and the database? Answer: checks the nonce of the group, manage_options and the allowed options list, then update_option() runs your sanitize callback, then it redirects back with settings-updated=true.
  3. Your sanitize callback refuses a value. What should it store, and how does the user find out? Answer: the old (saved) value, and add_settings_error() queues a message the page prints above the form.

  • Lesson exercises. 5.3: Exercises 1 to 3 (the date validator, esc_js, a prepared count); Exercise 4 is a stretch. 5.4: Exercises 1 to 3 (wp option patch, a stylesheet on one page, a top-level menu); Exercise 4 is a stretch.
  • Both Quick Quizzes on the lesson pages (answers in the Answer Key).
  • Journal: both entries. The 5.3 prompt traces one untrusted value through a handler you wrote; the 5.4 prompt lists everything the site stores and who owns it (Session 11 adds a table to that list).
  • Labs not reached: labs/module-10/l5_3-security/prepared_search_starter.php, labs/module-10/l5_3-security/debug_book_search.php, labs/module-10/l5_4-settings-api/debug_newsletter_sanitize.php, and after the project labs/module-10/l5_4-settings-api/settings_probe_starter.php.

If You Run Long or Short

Running long: what to protect and what to cut first
  • Protect: two attacks shown for real; the hardened save; the 5.4 round trip with one value refused.
  • Cut first (saves 3m): the 5.3 sanitizer step (the workbook's worked example covers the same functions).
  • Cut second (saves 3m): 5.4's half-array mistake: say the one sentence, point at Common Mistakes 3.
  • Cut third (saves 7m): the 5.3 project Step 2: the stock action and its forged request go home together.
Running short: what to add
  • Lesson 5.3's Exercise 4 together: a capability-gated bulk change, run as Maria, then as Devon.
  • Lesson 5.4's Common Mistakes 1 live: swap the group for the slug, save, read "not in the allowed options list", swap back.
  • Lesson 5.4's Exercise 4: the settings in /wp/v2/settings, and the schema that makes REST refuse a string for an integer.
Instructor Kit · Facilitator Guide

Session 11: Custom Tables, Shortcodes and Block Setup

How to teach Session 11. Finish Module 5 with shortcodes that return escaped HTML and a custom events table built with dbDelta(), read and written with $wpdb and migrated by a schema version, then open Module 6: Node 24, create-block in the existing plugin, the @wordpress/scripts build and its manifest, and the Blocks feature that registers the Book Card.

2 lessons 3 hrs session Lessons 5.5–6.1 Session 11 of 18 · Part 2

How to Use This Guide

  • Same rhythm for both lessons: frame → live demo (you type, they type along) → guided lab (a kit lab, new practice) → start the lesson's own project. Exercises, quiz and journal are homework.
  • Every command below was run to produce the output printed under it, on WordPress 7.1.3 / PHP 8.5: the 5.5 demo on the site as Lesson 5.4 leaves it (after:lesson_17), the 6.1 demo on the site as Lesson 5.5 leaves it, with Node 24 in the node:24 container (create-block, npm install and the build really ran).
  • Type the short things, copy the long ones: the WP-CLI, sed and npm lines are typed; BookShortcode.php, EventsTable.php, the Activator, the test scripts, package.json and Blocks.php are copied from the lesson pages and read aloud.
  • Keep lesson_18.html and lesson_19.html open. Labs live in labs/module-11/: _starter files and folders are handouts, _solution ones are yours.
  • Session 11 is the hinge between PHP and JavaScript: the first half finishes Module 5 (data), the second starts Module 6 (blocks). Lesson 6.1 needs Node 24 and a 540 MB npm install: the warm-up starts that download.
The #1 risk of Session 11: the npm install eats Lesson 6.1

Twenty laptops downloading 540 MB of build tools at once over venue Wi-Fi can take longer than the whole lesson. Before: Session 10's bring list asked for Node 24; email again two days ahead. In the warm-up: every learner creates pagesco-books/package.json from Lesson 6.1 (it does not depend on Lesson 5.5) and starts npm install in a second terminal, so the download runs through Lesson 5.5. In the demo: if a laptop is still installing, the learner follows on the projector and builds at the project start. The shelf_label lab needs no Node at all (its build/ is prebuilt).

Before the Session

  • ☐ Homework check by email: the site at the end of Lesson 5.4 (nine features, wp option get pagesco_books_settings prints the defaults), and node --version printing v24 (or docker pull node:24 done).
  • ☐ Run the kit check once: python3 labs/check_labs.py module-11 (19 results in about two minutes; every line PASS).
  • ☐ Projector machine at the end of Lesson 5.4 (after:lesson_17), Node 24 installed, npm install for pagesco-books already done once at home (so the npm cache is warm), VS Code, two terminals, the post editor in a browser tab.
  • ☐ Board: the storage table (content = post type, groups = taxonomy, site-wide values = option, many uniform rows = custom table); the kit-workshop-shelf drawing: src/blocks → npm run build → build/blocks + manifest → Blocks feature on init → the editor and the front end.
  • ☐ Print or share: the workbook, sticky notes.
Known traps of Session 11
SymptomCauseFix
The shortcode's output appears above the pageThe callback echoesBuild a string and return it (ob_start() / ob_get_clean() for template-style HTML).
A new column never appearsschema() changed, DB_VERSION not raisedRaise DB_VERSION; the next request migrates.
Unknown column after renaming a column in schema()dbDelta() only adds; the old column stays and the new one is emptyAn explicit ALTER TABLE step for that version.
npx asks "Ok to proceed?" and seems to hangThe first create-block downloadAnswer y.

"The specified manifest file does not exist." above every pageNo build/ (fresh checkout, npm never ran)npm install && npm run build in the plugin folder.
The editor shows the old block after a changebuild/ is stalenpm run build, or keep npm start running.
npm or node not found in Ubuntu on WindowsNode installed in Windows, not in WSLInstall Node inside WSL (nvm), or use the node:24 image.
EACCES errors from npm in the docker run lineThe container ran as root, or HOME is not writableThe lesson's --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" -e HOME=/tmp.

Lesson Plans

5.5

Shortcodes, $wpdb & Custom Tables

65 min
Objectives (from the lesson page)
  • Register shortcodes with add_shortcode() whose callbacks return escaped HTML, with attributes handled by shortcode_atts()
  • Decide when a custom table is the right storage, and when post types, meta, taxonomies or options are
  • Create and upgrade a table with dbDelta() and a schema version stored in an option
  • Read and write rows with $wpdb: insert(), update(), delete(), get_row(), get_var(), get_results(), always through prepare() or format arrays
  • Remove the table and its version option in uninstall.php
Timing in the room
10mFrame: the placeholder card; when a custom table is right
25mLive demo: BookShortcode, attributes, the table, a row's life, a schema change without a version
15mGuided lab: wishlist_table_starter.php
15mStart the lesson project: Steps 1 and 2
Mental model to say

"Picture the shop window with a small card that reads 'Book of the Month goes here'. Whoever dresses the window does not need to know the price or the stock; every morning someone swaps the card for the real book. A shortcode is that card: the editor writes [pagesco_book id="30"], and on every page view your callback swaps it for the book's current title, price and stock."

Then the second picture: "Post types, meta, taxonomies and options give you admin screens, REST, revisions and export for free. A table of your own gives all that up, so it is the last choice, for many rows with the same few fields, queried by those fields: events, later bookings and holds." And the one rule for both: values reach SQL only through placeholders.

Live demo (you type, they follow)

On the site as Lesson 5.4 leaves it.

  1. A shortcode returns, never echoes (4m). "A shortcode is a placeholder card in the shop window." Learners copy src/Shortcodes/BookShortcode.php; read render() aloud: shortcode_atts(), absint(), a check that it is a published book, every value escaped, a returned string. 	echo $case, "\n  => '", do_shortcode( $case ), "'\n";
}

    A page that is not a book, no attribute at all: an empty string, never an error message in a public page. Upper-case names are lowercased; undeclared attributes dropped.

  5. A row's whole life (4m). "Six methods, every value through a placeholder." The lesson's script in the WordPress root: 
    <?php
use PagesCo\Books\EventsTable;

global $wpdb;
$table = EventsTable::name();

$id = EventsTable::add( 'Test event', '2027-10-31 12:00:00', 'Back office' );
echo "insert: new ID $id\n";

$row = $wpdb->get_row( $wpdb->prepare( 'SELECT title, location FROM %i WHERE id = %d', $table, $id ) );
echo "get_row: {$row->title} in the {$row->location}\n";

$changed = $wpdb->update( $table, array( 'location' => 'Café' ), array( 'id' => $id ), array( '%s' ), array( '%d' ) );
echo "update: $changed row(s) changed\n";

echo 'prepare: ', $wpdb->prepare( 'SELECT COUNT(*) FROM %i WHERE location = %s', $table, "Children's corner" ), "\n";

$deleted = $wpdb->delete( $table, array( 'id' => $id ), array( '%d' ) );
echo "delete: $deleted row(s) deleted\n";
echo 'rows left: ', $wpdb->get_var( $wpdb->prepare( 'SELECT COUNT(*) FROM %i', $table ) ), "\n";

get_row: Test event in the Back office
update: 1 row(s) changed
prepare: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM `wp_pagesco_events` WHERE location = 'Children\'s corner'
delete: 1 row(s) deleted
rows left: 0
    Point at the prepare: line: the table in backticks from %i, the apostrophe escaped. Then rm events-crud.php.
  6. Mistake: a schema change without a version (4m). "The shop wants a host per event. Add the column, reload, and..."

1
host_columns

    0 host columns: maybe_upgrade() only runs when DB_VERSION is higher. Take the line out again (sed -i '/host varchar(100)/d' ...). The project does it right.
Three mistakes to expect, and how to coach each
  • A shortcode that echoes. Coach: "Where does echo print, and when does the callback run?" (the open_hours lab shows it).
  • Hard-coding wp_ or interpolating values into SQL. Coach: "Who controls this string? $wpdb->prefix is WordPress's; anything from a visitor goes through a placeholder." (Self-check Q3.)
  • A schema change without DB_VERSION, or a rename expected from dbDelta(). Coach with the two mistakes of the lesson: dbDelta only ADDS, and only when asked. (Self-check Q5.)

Checks for understanding
  • What must a shortcode callback do with its HTML? Answer: return it, escaped; never echo.
  • When is a custom table the right storage? Answer: many rows with the same few fields, queried by those fields, not edited as content.

6.1

Block Development Setup

80 min
Objectives (from the lesson page)
  • Describe a block type as WordPress sees it: block.json metadata, an editor script with edit and save, styles, and (later) PHP rendering
  • Scaffold a block into an existing plugin with npx @wordpress/create-block and --no-plugin, and read every generated file
  • Build blocks with @wordpress/scripts, and say what each file in build/ is for, including index.asset.php and the blocks manifest
  • Register all built blocks from a plugin feature with wp_register_block_types_from_metadata_collection()
  • Recognize the setup mistakes that cost beginners an afternoon: a second plugin by accident, a missing build, and stale build files
Timing in the room
10mFrame: a kit, a workshop and a shelf; the four parts of a block type
35mLive demo: Node, create-block, package.json and the build, the manifest, the Blocks feature, two mistakes
15mGuided lab: shelf_label_starter/
20mStart the lesson project: Step 1 and a look in the editor
Mental model to say

"The source files in src/blocks/book-card/ are a flat-pack kit: modern JavaScript with JSX and SCSS that no browser reads as is. The build is the workshop: @wordpress/scripts assembles the kit into plain JavaScript and CSS in build/blocks/book-card/. WordPress only ever looks at the shelf, the build/ folder, through the registration call in your plugin. Change the kit and nothing happens on the shelf until the workshop runs again."

Then the four parts on the board: block.json (metadata, read by PHP and the editor) · edit (the editing view, a React component) · save (the HTML stored in post_content) · styles (and later a PHP render). "A static block's front end needs no JavaScript: visitors get the stored HTML."

Live demo (you type, they follow)

    Every one a block.json in wp-includes/blocks plus prebuilt JavaScript. A static block's front end needs no JavaScript at all.

Differentiation

Closing

Exit ticket (3 questions, no notes, 4 minutes)
  1. Why must a shortcode callback return its HTML instead of echoing it? Answer: it runs while the content is filtered, before the page is printed (in a block theme before the <head>); echoed output lands outside the content.
  2. You add a column to schema(). What else must change, and why? Answer: DB_VERSION must go up, so maybe_upgrade() runs install() on the next request; updates do not rerun activation.
  3. Name the path of the Book Card from your files to the editor. Answer: src/blocks/book-card → npm run build → build/blocks + blocks-manifest.php → the Blocks feature registers them on init → the editor (and the front end gets the saved HTML and style-index.css).
Homework (about 2 to 3 hours)
  • Finish both lesson projects. 5.5: Steps 3 and 4 (EventsShortcode, the seeding script, the Events page with five events). 6.1: Steps 3 and 4 (the front end, the final check). Session 12 starts from exactly this site: thirteen features and a built Book Card.
  • Lesson exercises. 5.5: Exercises 1 to 3; Exercise 4 is a stretch. 6.1: Exercises 1 to 3; Exercise 4 is a stretch.
  • Both Quick Quizzes and both journal entries.
  • Labs not reached: labs/module-11/l5_5-custom-tables/open_hours_starter/, labs/module-11/l5_5-custom-tables/debug_events_report.php, labs/module-11/l6_1-block-setup/core_blocks_tour_starter.sh, labs/module-11/l6_1-block-setup/debug_block_registration.php.
Bring list for Session 12
  • The site at the end of Lesson 6.1: npm run build works in pagesco-books, the Book Card (book icon) is in the inserter, /events/ lists five events.
  • Node 24 (or the node:24 image); the project folder with labs/; the journal and the workbook.

If You Run Long or Short

Running long: what to protect and what to cut first
  • Protect: a working build and a registered Book Card; the versioned migration; a shortcode that returns.
  • Cut first (saves 3m): the attribute cases of 5.5 (self-check Q1 covers them).
  • Cut second (saves 3m): 6.1's stale-build mistake: one sentence.
  • Cut third (saves 7m): 5.5 project Step 2: uninstall.php goes home.
Running short: what to add
  • Lesson 5.5's Common Mistakes 3 live: dbDelta() "renaming" a column adds a second one.
  • Lesson 6.1's Exercise 2 (your block among core's widgets) and Exercise 3 (the text domain survives the build).
  • npm start on the projector: change the editor text, reload the editor, watch it change.
Instructor Kit · Facilitator Guide

Session 12: Static and Dynamic Blocks

How to teach the session where the Book Card becomes a real block and the shop gets its first dynamic one: where a static block keeps each attribute and why its stored HTML is a contract, then a render.php that queries the catalog on every view and core blocks bound to the books' own data.

2 lessons 3 hrs session Lessons 6.2–6.3 Session 12 of 18 · Part 2

How to Use This Guide

  • Same rhythm for both lessons: frame (the goal and one mental model) → live demo (you type, they type along) → guided lab (a kit lab, new practice on the lesson's ideas) → start the lesson's own project. The lesson exercises, quiz and journal are homework.
  • Every command below was run on WordPress 7.1.3 / PHP 8.5 to produce the output printed under it: Lesson 6.2's demo on the site exactly as Lesson 6.1 left it (after:lesson_19), Lesson 6.3's on the site after Lesson 6.2 (after:lesson_20). Browser-only results (the editor's validation messages) are quoted from the lesson page, which recorded them in a real 7.1 editor. Ask for a prediction before every run.
  • This session is half JavaScript files the editor runs and half PHP the server runs. Learners copy the .js, .json and .scss files from the lesson pages (they are long, and the lessons explain them line by line); the room's time goes to the PHP side, the stored markup and the mental models, which are what people get wrong alone.
  • Labs live in labs/module-12/ (learners keep the folder in their project folder, next to compose.yaml): _starter files and folders are handouts, _solution files and folders are yours. The block labs need no Node: the Next Events block registers a block.json and a render.php from PHP and is tested with do_blocks().
  • Part 2, Session 4 of 10. Teal blocks are hands-on, amber blocks are watch-outs. Lesson codes (6.2, 6.3) match the course site.
The #1 risk of Session 12: the build eats the session

Both lessons change files that only matter after npm run build, and every laptop builds differently: native Node 24, the node:24 container, a stale npm start in another terminal. Ten learners with a missing build means ten editors saying "This block has encountered an error". Before: the warm-up's W3 to W5 are a build check; anyone whose ls wp-content/plugins/pagesco-books/build/blocks does not show the manifest gets a partner. In the room: you type every file, and the room may watch instead of typing (the files are on the lesson pages); what they must type is the PHP (render.php, BookBindings.php) and the commands. After: the two lesson projects need the built blocks; send the Before the Next Lesson checks home in writing.

Before the Session

  • ☐ Projector site at after:lesson_19: the end of Lesson 6.1 (the 6.1 Book Card, npm run build working). Know your build command: native npm run build in wordpress/wp-content/plugins/pagesco-books, or Lesson 6.1's docker run --rm ... node:24 npm run build. Keep a second terminal for the WP-CLI container shell (docker compose run --rm wpcli sh).
  • ☐ Rehearse once: Lesson 6.2's sections on a scratch copy of the site (the deprecation step in particular: reload Card test, read the Console, add deprecated.js, reload again), then Lesson 6.3's render.php and BookBindings. The whole session's demo takes three builds.
  • ☐ Files to hand out: labs/module-12/ WITHOUT the *_solution.* files and the card_price_solution/ and next_events_solution/ folders. Run the kit check once: python3 labs/check_labs.py module-12 (15 results, about two minutes).
  • ☐ Projector: VS Code on pagesco-dev at a large font, the browser with the editor (admin / password), View Source, and the developer tools' Console; lesson_20.html and lesson_21.html in tabs (their screenshots show the Settings and Styles panels if your editor misbehaves).
  • ☐ Board, before learners arrive: a two-column table HTML (source + selector) | comment (no source, only if not default), and the line static = printed card · dynamic = departure board · binding = shelf label.
Known traps of this session
SymptomCauseFix
"This block has encountered an error" or the old card after a changeNo build since the change, or the build failednpm run build in the plugin folder; read its last line. npm start keeps building while you work.
Notices about register_collection / blocks-manifest.php above wp-admin, the editor brokenbuild/ is missing (Lesson 6.1's trap)Build once; never commit or copy the plugin without build/.
"Block contains unexpected or invalid content"save() changed for content that exists (or a selector catches a nested element, Mistake 2)A deprecated entry with the old attributes, supports and save; or delete test posts while still developing.
Warning: Undefined array key "title" above the doctypePHP read an HTML-sourced attribute from $block['attrs']Read the HTML with the HTML API, or make the value a comment attribute, or make the block dynamic.
Warning: Undefined array key "count" inside the pagerender.php read an attribute that has no defaultisset() or ??; and fix it in src/, not in build/ (the next build wipes build/).
A bound paragraph shows "Author" or "Price"Wrong meta key, a key without show_in_rest, or a source without uses_contextget_registered_meta_keys( 'post', 'book' ); check uses_context; choose fallbacks that look wrong.
List items print "Stock" instead of the valueWordPress older than 7.1Bind paragraphs instead (the lesson's version note).

Timing

Questions and answers
  1. W1 (Lesson 5.5). A shortcode callback ends with echo $html; instead of return $html;. What goes wrong? Answer: The HTML appears at the top of the content (wherever the filter runs), not where the shortcode is: shortcodes RETURN their output. The [pagesco_events] callback returns it.
  2. W2 (Lesson 5.5). Why does EventsTable::find() build its SQL with $wpdb->prepare() even though only the plugin calls it? Answer: Because the location comes from shortcode attributes, REST arguments (Lesson 7.2) and anyone who edits a post: every value goes through placeholders, every time.
  3. W3 (Lesson 6.1). Where does npm run build write, and which file does WordPress read to register the plugin's blocks? Answer: Into build/blocks/ (blocks-manifest.php and book-card on the projector site), and build/blocks/blocks-manifest.php, read by wp_register_block_types_from_metadata_collection() in the Blocks feature.
  4. W4 (Lesson 6.1). You add a second block folder in src/blocks/ and build. What PHP do you add to register it? Answer: None: the manifest lists every built block and the Blocks feature registers them all. Today's Book List proves it.
  5. W5 (Lesson 6.1). You edited src/blocks/book-card/edit.js, reloaded the editor, and nothing changed. First question? Answer: Did you build? The editor loads build/blocks/book-card/index.js. npm start rebuilds on every save while you work.

On the projector site the build folder holds:

ls wp-content/plugins/pagesco-books/build/blocks
blocks-manifest.php  book-card

Anyone who sees no book-card folder builds now (or pairs). Laptops that cannot build at all do today's PHP labs and type the PHP parts of the demos; the JavaScript halves wait for the build at home.

Lesson Plans

6.2

Static Blocks: Attributes, Controls & Supports

65 min
Objectives (from the lesson page)
  • Declare attributes in block.json and choose where each one is stored: in the saved HTML (source and selector) or in the block's comment
  • Make text editable on the canvas with RichText and save it with RichText.Content
  • Add settings to the block sidebar with InspectorControls and components from @wordpress/components
  • Opt into color, spacing and typography block supports and read the classes and styles they save
  • Explain block validation, and change save safely with a deprecated entry and migrate
Timing in the room
10mFrame: the printed card with a sticky note; HTML or comment; the stored HTML is a contract
25mLive demo: three attributes, the stored post and PHP's view, supports, validation and a deprecation, Mistake 1
15mGuided lab: attribute_sources_starter.php
15mStart the lesson project: Step 1, the Hobbit staff pick
Mental model to say

Hold up a printed shop card: "A static block in a post is this card with a sticky note on the back. The printed side is the HTML: every visitor sees it, and the bookseller's words are printed right on it. The sticky note is the comment JSON: the few settings that are not words, such as heading level 2. The editor reads both to rebuild the card for editing. PHP can read the sticky note easily; to find the words it would have to read the print."

Then the board table: source + selector = in the HTML (title, author, the link's href); no source = in the comment, and only when it differs from the default (headingLevel, showBadge, colors). "Lesson 1.3's pagesco_book_card() took the same data as arguments. The difference is WHERE a block keeps them."

Then the contract: "Every time the editor opens a post it runs your CURRENT save() with the attributes it read and compares the result with the stored HTML. Different means invalid. Once content exists, save() may not change without describing the old version: a deprecation."

Live demo (you type, they follow)

Lesson 6.2's own files and commands, typed live. The block files are long: show them on the lesson page, paste them into VS Code, and spend the time on what each part STORES. Outputs come from the site exactly as Lesson 6.1 left it.

  1. Before: the 6.1 card (2m). "Lesson 6.1's card has no data of its own. Ask WordPress which attributes it has." Type the registry one-liner from the lesson in the WP-CLI container (docker compose run --rm wpcli sh): 
    wp eval 'echo implode( ", ", array_keys( WP_Block_Type_Registry::get_instance()->get_registered( "pagesco/book-card" )->get_attributes() ) ), "\n";'
    lock, metadata, className, style
    Four attributes WordPress adds to every block, none of the card's own. Write HTML or comment? on the board.
  2. Three sourced attributes (6m). "A bookseller types the title, the author and why she loves the book, right on the card." Replace block.json with the lesson's first version (show the attributes part on the projector), then edit.js (RichText for each field, allowedFormats), save.js (RichText.Content) and style.scss, all from the lesson page, and build in the plugin folder:

Add the lesson's showBadge version (block.json, edit.js, save.js, style.scss), build, and reload Card test in the editor with the Console open (F12). The card shows Block contains unexpected or invalid content; the Console says why:

Block validation: Block validation failed for `pagesco/book-card` (Object).

Content generated by `save` function:

<div class="wp-block-pagesco-book-card has-sage-background-color has-background has-small-font-size" style="…"><p class="wp-block-pagesco-book-card__badge">Staff pick</p><a class="wp-block-pagesco-book-card__link" …
