Checks for understanding

Ask during the demo and the lab:

  • Should Pages & Co.'s next redesign be headless? Answer: probably not: one website, staff who edit in the block editor; headless pays for several front ends or an app.
  • Where does a client's API key for an AI provider go? Answer: an environment variable or constant on the server (the lesson's quiz Q3), never in the front end or the plugin.
  • A model asks to run pagesco/check-stock for Devon. What decides? Answer: the ability's permission callback, run as Devon: it refuses.

Workbook self-check, items Q7 to Q12.

Answers: Q7 Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://shop.example; no: WordPress echoes any origin, so a page anywhere may READ the answers, but the permission callbacks still refuse (a visitor gets 401 from /holds); Q8 C) Know which fields are HTML: decode the stored-escaped name once to text (DOMParser), then put it on the page with textContent; Q9 A) Plumbing: the AI client (wp_ai_client_prompt()), the Connectors screen and a switch to turn AI off; no model, no provider and no core feature; Q10 wp-includes/ai-client.php: only the file that defines the function; no core screen, block or feature calls the AI client; Q11 D) wpab__pagesco__check-stock; Q12 a secret that was committed once and deleted later is still in the history, and anyone who clones the repository can read it; -S lists every commit that added or removed the string, on every branch. Full set with explanations in the Answer Key.

Differentiation

Support: learners still finishing the project spend the guided lab on Milestone 9 or 10 instead; the lab and the 9.2 project wait for after the submission.

Stretch: the lesson's Exercise 4 (a second ability as a tool) and the Going Further static build; the kit's ai_readiness lab.

Closing

Final submission (one week from today)

The lesson's submission checklist, read aloud and in the workbook:

  • git tag -n in wordpress/wp-content lists release-3, and git status is clean
  • pagesco-books.zip (1.2.0) and pagesco.zip (1.2.0) are kept with your release notes
  • The output of composer lint, the PHPUnit run and both smoke tests is saved in your write-up or next to it
  • The rehearsal server runs 1.2.0, has a My holds page, and its backup from before the deploy is in backups/
  • RESERVE-AND-PICKUP.md maps every requirement to the code, lists your decisions and next steps
  • If you share the project publicly (a portfolio, a Git host), share the code and screenshots only: never .env, database dumps or passwords

Agree how it arrives (a link to a private repository you can read, or a ZIP of the wp-content repository's git archive release-3 plus the two release ZIPs and the write-up). The grading run and scoring sheet are in final-assessment.html.

Exit ticket (3 questions, no notes, 4 minutes)
  1. Which of your checks proves that another customer's hold cannot be cancelled, and which one cannot prove it? Answer: HoldsTest's test_only_the_customer (and holds-check.php) proves it; the smoke test cannot: it plays one customer.
  2. Code goes up, content stays: name one thing of Reserve & Pick Up for each. Answer: up: the plugin and theme 1.2.0 (the ZIPs); created on live: the My holds page and the shoptest account (and the holds table, by the code itself).
  3. What will you build next with WordPress, and which lesson will you reread first? Answer: their own (next-plan.txt).
Homework (about 2 to 3 hours)
  • Finish the final project: whatever is left of Milestones 7 to 9, Milestone 10 (RESERVE-AND-PICKUP.md, the lesson's outline) and the submission checklist; due one week from today.
  • Lesson 9.1: the exercises (collect over REST, tell the shop, the personal data exporter), the Quick Quiz, the journal prompt (compare the site you planned in Lesson 1.1 with the one you launched).
  • Lesson 9.2: project steps 1 to 3 and the rest of step 5; Exercises 1 to 3 (Exercise 4 is a stretch); the Quick Quiz; the last journal entry, which answers the first one's two questions again.
  • Optional: labs/module-18/l9_2-next-steps/ai_readiness_starter.php, labs/module-18/l9_2-next-steps/publish_scan_starter.sh, labs/module-18/l9_2-next-steps/debug_headless_client.php; for the release, labs/module-18/l9_1-final-project/version_audit_starter.php and labs/module-18/l9_1-final-project/smoke_rest_starter.sh.
  • Before you stop: npx @wordpress/env stop, docker compose stop in pagesco-dev and pagesco-live (both keep their data).
Course close (in the last 10 minutes)
  • Look back (2m): the first exit ticket of Session 1 ("where does your own code go?") against today's feature. Name three things the room can do now that it could not in Session 1.
  • Evaluation (3m): the course evaluation, before anyone leaves.
  • What comes next (2m): the lesson's Looking Ahead: the glossary, cheat sheet, common errors and troubleshooting pages as the reference; React + WordPress Mastery for headless; the Freelance Launchpad for client work; one meetup and one Make team. Remind them that results and certificates follow the scoring of the final project.

If You Run Long or Short

Running long: what to protect and what to cut first
  • Protect: the showcase for every learner; the ZIP check; the code-only deploy rule; the model call for Maria and Devon.
  • Cut first (saves 15m): the 9.2 guided lab; it goes home.
  • Cut second (saves 5m): the Connectors step of the demo; the lesson's card shows it.
  • Cut third (saves 5m): Milestone 7's accessibility walk; with axe at home, results in the write-up.
Running short: what to add
  • Common Mistake 1's rollback live on your rehearsal server: a ZIP without src/Holds, the critical error, wp --skip-plugins plugin install ... --force.
  • Lesson 9.2's storefront served from a second origin (npx serve -l 3000 wordpress/storefront) with the browser's Network panel open.
  • A five-minute career round: each learner names the path from the lesson's table that fits them and the one piece of their project they would show first.
